//! Aggregate deltas, derived rebuilds and the device overlay.
use super::runner::Runner;
use super::write::Origin;
use crate::error::{MeterKind, RuntimeError};
use crate::schema::{Maintain, MaintainKind, maintained_id};
#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
use crate::schema::materialize_optional_fields;
#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
use crate::rows::{Bounds, Dir};
use crate::value::{I53_MAX, I53_MIN, Value};
use crate::value::canonical_json;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

const GLOBAL: &str = "$global";

fn target_group_key(maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> Vec<Value> {
    if maintain.by.is_empty() { vec![Value::Bool(true)] } else { key.to_vec() }
}

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
fn has_legacy_maintained_reference(
    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
) -> bool {
    match kind {
        crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table } => ids.get(table).is_some_and(|ids| !ids.is_empty()),
        crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner)
        | crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. }
        | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => has_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, ids),
        _ => false,
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(
    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
    value: &mut Value,
    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
) -> bool {
    match (kind, value) {
        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => {
            let Some(next) = ids.get(table).and_then(|ids| ids.get(id)) else { return false };
            *id = next.clone();
            true
        }
        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, value, ids),
        (crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of, .. } | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),
        _ => false,
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
type LegacyIdentities = Vec<(String, Vec<(String, Vec<(crate::schema::ColumnType, Value)>)>)>;

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
type LegacyIdentityMap = BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, Vec<(crate::schema::ColumnType, Value)>>>;

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
fn collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(
    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
    value: &Value,
    definitions: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<crate::schema::ColumnType>>,
    identities: &mut LegacyIdentityMap,
) {
    match (kind, value) {
        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(old)) => {
            let Some(kinds) = definitions.get(table) else { return };
            if identities.get(table).is_some_and(|ids| ids.contains_key(old)) { return; }
            let Some(values) = crate::json_codec::from_text::<Vec<Value>>(old).ok()
                .filter(|values| values.len() == kinds.len()) else { return };
            let key: Vec<_> = kinds.iter().cloned().zip(values).collect();
            identities.entry(table.clone()).or_default().insert(old.clone(), key.clone());
            for (kind, value) in &key {
                collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(kind, value, definitions, identities);
            }
        }
        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) =>
            collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(inner, value, definitions, identities),
        (crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of, .. } | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
            for value in values { collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(of, value, definitions, identities); },
        _ => {}
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
fn insert_sequence_identity(
    target: &str,
    old: String,
    key: Vec<(crate::schema::ColumnType, Value)>,
    definitions: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<crate::schema::ColumnType>>,
    identities: &mut LegacyIdentityMap,
) {
    if identities.get(target).is_some_and(|ids| ids.contains_key(&old)) { return; }
    identities.entry(target.to_owned()).or_default().insert(old, key.clone());
    for (kind, value) in &key {
        collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(kind, value, definitions, identities);
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
fn settle_legacy_maintained_ids(
    legacy: &LegacyIdentities,
    base: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>, RuntimeError> {
    let mut ids = base.clone();
    let identity_count = legacy.iter().map(|(_, rows)| rows.len()).sum::<usize>();
    for _ in 0..=identity_count.saturating_add(1) {
        let mut next_ids = base.clone();
        for (target, rows) in legacy {
            let target_ids = next_ids.entry(target.clone()).or_default();
            for (old, key) in rows {
                let key: Vec<_> = key.iter().map(|(kind, value)| {
                    let mut value = value.clone();
                    rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &mut value, &ids);
                    value
                }).collect();
                let next = maintained_id(&key);
                if old != &next { target_ids.insert(old.clone(), next); }
            }
        }
        if next_ids == ids { return Ok(next_ids); }
        ids = next_ids;
    }
    Err(RuntimeError::Schema("legacy aggregate identity references form a cycle".into()))
}

impl Runner<'_> {
    // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — no predicted delta enters receipt-derived state.
    pub(super) fn defer_receipt_maintain(&self, m: &Maintain) -> bool {
        self.device && self.schema.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&m.target)
    }

    // Cache ordinary group keys once per target/query. Predicates and receipt
    // fields are never evaluated; unknown/computed keys conservatively freeze
    // the target. An unpinned read is incomplete if any group is dirty, while
    // each returned row still decides independently whether to recount.
    #[inline(never)]
    pub(super) fn receipt_maintain_pending(&mut self, m: &Maintain, group: Option<&[Value]>) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        if !self.defer_receipt_maintain(m) { return Ok(false); }
        if !self.receipt_pending_groups.contains_key(&m.target) {
            let fields = if let Some(k) = &m.row_key { vec![k.source_key.clone()] }
                else { m.by.iter().map(|f| m.aliases.get(f).unwrap_or(f).clone()).collect() };
            let mut groups = self.receipt_overlay_groups(&m.source, &fields, !m.computed.is_empty())?;
            if let Some(k) = &m.row_key {
                let member = self.receipt_overlay_groups(&k.table, std::slice::from_ref(&k.member_key), false)?;
                groups = groups.zip(member).map(|(mut source, member)| { source.extend(member); source });
            }
            self.receipt_pending_groups.insert(m.target.clone(), groups);
        }
        let dirty = self.receipt_pending_groups[&m.target].as_ref().is_none_or(|keys|
            group.map_or(!keys.is_empty(), |group| keys.iter().any(|key| key == group)));
        if dirty {
            self.value_source_incomplete = true;
            self.components.note(|frame| frame.pending = true);
        }
        Ok(dirty)
    }

    fn receipt_overlay_groups(&self, table: &str, fields: &[String], computed: bool) -> Result<Option<Vec<Vec<Value>>>, RuntimeError> {
        if !self.tx.has_provisional(table)? { return Ok(Some(Vec::new())); }
        if computed || fields.iter().any(|f| self.schema.receipt_dependencies.get(table).is_some_and(|owned| owned.contains(f))) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        self.tx.provisional_groups(table, fields)
    }

    // Recover a read's parent/group from the pinned index. A member point uses
    // one ordinary-key lookup; a scan without the parent stays conservative.
    pub(super) fn receipt_read_group(&mut self, m: &Maintain, index: &str, key: &[Value]) -> Result<Option<Vec<Value>>, RuntimeError> {
        if !self.defer_receipt_maintain(m) { return Ok(None); }
        let columns = self.schema.tables[&m.target].indexes[index].columns();
        let pinned = |field: &str| columns.iter().position(|c| c == field).and_then(|i| key.get(i)).cloned();
        if let Some(k) = &m.row_key {
            if let Some(parent) = pinned(&k.member_key) { return Ok(Some(vec![parent])); }
            if let Some(id) = pinned("member").or_else(|| pinned("id")) {
                let row = self.metered_scan(|r, scope| r.tx.get(scope, &k.table, id.as_str()?))?;
                return Ok(row.and_then(|row| row.field(&k.member_key).ok().cloned()).map(|v| vec![v]));
            }
            return Ok(None);
        }
        Ok(m.by.iter().map(|f| pinned(f)).collect())
    }

    pub(super) fn maintain(&mut self, source: &str, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.receipt_pending_groups.clear();
        // Inserts ordinarily charge their actual aggregate work. A deferred
        // predicate cannot select that work on a device, so use the same public
        // worst-case reservation as update/delete before skipping it. Already
        // prepaid writes must not pay twice.
        if self.device && !self.maintain_prepaid && self.schema.maintains.iter().any(|m|
            m.source == source && m.private.is_none() && m.row_key.is_none() && (self.schema.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&m.target) || self.schema.tables[&m.target].sync.is_none())) {
            self.reserve_maintains(source, &self.schema.tables[source])?;
        }
        self.maintain_row_views(source, old, new)?;
        let maintains = self.schema.maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.source == source && maintain.row_key.is_none());
        for maintain in maintains {
            if self.defer_receipt_maintain(maintain) || (self.device && self.schema.tables[&maintain.target].sync.is_none()) { continue; }
            let source_bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.source]);
            let target = &self.schema.tables[&maintain.target];
            let bytes = source_bytes.saturating_mul(2).saturating_add(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(target).saturating_mul(16 + 4 * target.indexes.len() as u64));
            let prepaid = self.maintain_prepaid;
            if maintain.private.is_some() && self.column_prepaid { self.maintain_prepaid = true; }
            let result = self.maintain_scratch(bytes, |runner| runner.maintain_one(maintain, old, new));
            self.maintain_prepaid = prepaid;
            result?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — reserve interpreted images, both keys, targets and index buffers before allocation; release transient ownership on every exit.
    pub(super) fn maintain_scratch<T>(&mut self, bytes: u64, work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
        if self.maintain_prepaid { return work(self); }
        self.meter.heap(bytes)?;
        let result = work(self);
        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = self.meter.used.heap_bytes.saturating_sub(bytes);
        result
    }

    fn maintain_one(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let table = self.schema.table(&maintain.source).expect("validated");
        let mut changes: Vec<(Vec<Value>, i128)> = Vec::new();
        for (image, direction) in [(old, -1), (new, 1)] {
            let Some(image) = image else { continue };
            self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, maintain.evaluation_steps())?;
            let image = crate::schema::row_image(image, table);
            if !maintain.selected(&image) { continue; }
            let key = maintain.source_key(&image);
            let change = delta(maintain, &image, direction)?;
            if let Some(existing) = changes.iter_mut().find(|(k, _)| *k == key) { existing.1 += change; }
            else { changes.push((key, change)); }
        }
        for (key, change) in changes {
            if let Some(retiring) = self.retiring.as_mut() {
                let entry = retiring.aggregates.entry((maintain.target.clone(), canonical_json(&key))).or_insert_with(|| (key, 0));
                entry.1 = entry.1.checked_add(change).ok_or_else(|| aggregate_overflow(maintain))?;
                continue;
            }
            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, None)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Apply a retirement's net aggregate changes, one per target row, in
    /// key order. Only a total the commit really ends with can overflow.
    pub(super) fn apply_retired_aggregates(&mut self, changes: BTreeMap<(String, String), (Vec<Value>, i128)>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let schema = self.schema;
        for ((target, _), (key, change)) in changes {
            let maintain = schema.maintain_for(&target).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing maintain for {target}")))?;
            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, None)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    pub(crate) fn rebuild_maintain_reported(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, report: &mut crate::store::adoption_report::AdoptionReport) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
        self.rebuilt_source_rows = 0;
        self.rebuild_maintain(maintain)?;
        let rows = self.rebuilt_source_rows;
        report.views.push(crate::store::adoption_report::ViewBuild { name: maintain.label(), rows, elapsed: started.elapsed() });
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Derive every legacy-to-digest aggregate id map to a fixed point, then
    /// rewrite typed references before rebuilding the target rows. The fixed
    /// point matters when one aggregate groups by a reference to another.
    /// Every pass is inside the adoption writer transaction, so no reader can
    /// observe a dangling intermediate reference.
    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    pub(crate) fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(&mut self, maintains: &[Maintain], previous: Option<&crate::schema::Schema>, activation_tx: Option<&crate::store::Tx<'_>>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        let mut legacy: LegacyIdentities = Vec::new();
        let mut definitions = BTreeMap::<String, Vec<crate::schema::ColumnType>>::new();
        for maintain in maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()) {
            let target = &self.schema.tables[&maintain.target];
            definitions.insert(maintain.target.clone(), maintain.group_fields().into_iter()
                .map(|field| target.columns[&field].clone()).collect());
        }
        if let Some(previous) = previous {
            for maintain in previous.maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()) {
                let target = &previous.tables[&maintain.target];
                definitions.insert(maintain.target.clone(), maintain.group_fields().into_iter()
                    .map(|field| target.columns[&field].clone()).collect());
            }
        }
        let mut sequence_identity_map = LegacyIdentityMap::new();
        for maintain in maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()) {
            // The durable legacy address is the predecessor's canonical
            // logical group tuple. Decode that address with predecessor types:
            // candidate projection may already have removed predecessor group
            // columns when adoption also changes the maintain declaration.
            let identity_schema = previous.unwrap_or(self.schema);
            let identity_maintain = identity_schema.maintain_for(&maintain.target)
                .filter(|old| old.private.is_none() && old.row_key.is_none())
                .unwrap_or(maintain);
            let identity_target = identity_schema.table(&maintain.target)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| &self.schema.tables[&maintain.target]);
            let fields: Vec<_> = identity_maintain.group_fields().into_iter().map(|field| {
                let kind = identity_target.columns.get(&field).expect("validated maintain group").clone();
                (field, kind)
            }).collect();
            let mut rows = Vec::new();
            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
            loop {
                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.target, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
                if page.is_empty() { break; }
                for (row, encoded) in page {
                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
                    let old = row.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
                    let address = crate::json_codec::from_text::<Vec<Value>>(&old).ok()
                        .filter(|key| key.len() == fields.len());
                    let values = match address {
                        Some(key) => key,
                        None => fields.iter().map(|(field, _)| Ok(row.field(field)?.clone()))
                            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, RuntimeError>>()?,
                    };
                    let key: Vec<_> = fields.iter().zip(values).map(|((_, kind), value)| (kind.clone(), value)).collect();
                    rows.push((old, key));
                }
            }
            legacy.push((maintain.target.clone(), rows));
            for old in self.tx.sequence_ids(&maintain.target)? {
                let values = crate::json_codec::from_text::<Vec<Value>>(&old).ok()
                    .filter(|key| key.len() == fields.len());
                if let Some(values) = values {
                    let key = fields.iter().zip(values).map(|((_, kind), value)| (kind.clone(), value)).collect();
                    insert_sequence_identity(&maintain.target, old, key, &definitions, &mut sequence_identity_map);
                }
            }
        }

        // A removed aggregate can leave parent-counter history even after its
        // derived rows and every allocating row are gone. The store marker
        // covers that retained custody too: translate it from predecessor
        // types now so reintroducing the same maintained target cannot revive
        // a legacy address under a current marker.
        if let Some(previous) = previous {
            for maintain in previous.maintains.iter().filter(|maintain|
                maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()
                    && !maintains.iter().any(|current| current.target == maintain.target)) {
                let target = &previous.tables[&maintain.target];
                let fields: Vec<_> = maintain.group_fields().into_iter().map(|field|
                    (field.clone(), target.columns[&field].clone())).collect();
                for old in self.tx.sequence_ids(&maintain.target)? {
                    let values = crate::json_codec::from_text::<Vec<Value>>(&old).ok()
                        .filter(|key| key.len() == fields.len());
                    if let Some(values) = values {
                        let key = fields.iter().zip(values).map(|((_, kind), value)| (kind.clone(), value)).collect();
                        insert_sequence_identity(&maintain.target, old, key, &definitions, &mut sequence_identity_map);
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        // Row references retain the established contract: only a stored
        // aggregate target proves an old address. Sequence custody is broader;
        // its parent key persists after target/source/child deletion, so its
        // independently decoded legacy tuple joins the same fixed point.
        let ids = settle_legacy_maintained_ids(&legacy, &BTreeMap::new())?;
        let sequence_legacy: LegacyIdentities = sequence_identity_map.into_iter()
            .map(|(target, rows)| (target, rows.into_iter().collect())).collect();
        let sequence_ids = settle_legacy_maintained_ids(&sequence_legacy, &ids)?;

        // Sequence counters are keyed by the referenced parent table and id,
        // independently of any surviving allocating row. Translate them from
        // the same target-specific maps before rows are rebuilt; colliding
        // old/current counters retain the larger high-water value.
        // @ref LLP 3000.007.003#3.0 — digest adoption re-keys dependent sequence custody in the same transaction.
        let mut rewritten = self.tx.rewrite_sequence_ids(&sequence_ids)?;

        // Release retention is part of the store: a hidden row or column may
        // still name an aggregate target that remains active through adoption.
        // Rewrite its image and reference ledger in this transaction too.
        rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(match activation_tx {
            Some(tx) => crate::store::dormant::rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(tx, &ids)?,
            None => 0,
        });

        let references: Vec<_> = self.schema.tables.iter().filter_map(|(name, table)| {
            let columns: Vec<_> = table.columns.iter().filter_map(|(column, kind)|
                has_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &ids).then(|| (column.clone(), kind.clone())))
                .collect();
            (!columns.is_empty()).then(|| (name.clone(), table.clone(), columns))
        }).collect();
        for (name, table, columns) in references {
            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
            loop {
                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &name, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
                if page.is_empty() { break; }
                for (old, encoded) in page {
                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
                    let mut next = old.clone();
                    let mut changed = false;
                    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next {
                        for (column, kind) in &columns {
                            let Some(value) = fields.get_mut(column) else { continue };
                            changed |= rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, value, &ids);
                        }
                    }
                    if changed {
                        self.tx.put(&name, &table, &next, Some(&old))?;
                        rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(rewritten)
    }

    /// Build one aggregate from the rows in the store: the target's rows go,
    /// then every source row contributes once. A schema change that adds or
    /// redefines a `maintain` calls this, so a count over existing rows is
    /// right from its first read (day two, LLP 2000.000 §11.2).
    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    pub(crate) fn rebuild_maintain(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let heap = self.meter.used.heap_bytes;
        let saved = self.column_rebuild;
        self.column_rebuild |= maintain.private.is_some();
        let result = self.rebuild_maintain_inner(maintain);
        self.column_rebuild = saved;
        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = heap;
        result
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    fn rebuild_maintain_inner(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        if maintain.row_key.is_some() { return self.rebuild_row_view(maintain); }
        let target = self.schema.table(&maintain.target).expect("validated");
        let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
        let target_bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(target).saturating_mul(16 + 4 * target.indexes.len() as u64);
        self.meter.heap(target_bytes.saturating_mul(256))?;
        loop {
            let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.target, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
            if page.is_empty() { break; }
            for (existing, key) in page {
                bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
                self.refuse_timeline_write(&maintain.target, crate::schema::Effect::Delete)?;
                let entries = self.tx.delete(&maintain.target, target, &existing)?;
                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
                self.row_changed(&maintain.target, Some(&existing), None, Origin::Maintained)?;
            }
        }
        let source = self.schema.table(&maintain.source).expect("validated");
        self.meter.heap(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(source).saturating_mul(256))?;
        let mut totals: BTreeMap<String, (Vec<Value>, i128)> = BTreeMap::new();
        bounds = Bounds::default();
        loop {
            let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.source, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
            if page.is_empty() { break; }
            for (mut image, key) in page {
                self.rebuilt_source_rows += 1;
                bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
                materialize_optional_fields(&mut image, source);
                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, maintain.evaluation_steps())?;
                if !maintain.selected(&image) { continue; }
                // @ref LLP 3000.028#6 — a total unique owner key has one contribution; backfill streams bounded pages instead of retaining all lifetime keys in a totals map.
                if maintain.own_keys.is_some() {
                    let heap = self.meter.used.heap_bytes;
                    self.meter.heap(target_bytes)?;
                    self.apply_aggregate(maintain, maintain.source_key(&image), 1, Some(true))?;
                    self.meter.used.heap_bytes = heap;
                    continue;
                }
                self.meter.heap(target_bytes)?;
                let key = maintain.source_key(&image);
                let change = delta(maintain, &image, 1)?;
                let entry = match totals.entry(canonical_json(&key)) {
                    std::collections::btree_map::Entry::Occupied(entry) => {
                        self.meter.used.heap_bytes -= target_bytes;
                        entry.into_mut()
                    }
                    std::collections::btree_map::Entry::Vacant(entry) => entry.insert((key, 0)),
                };
                entry.1 = entry.1.checked_add(change).ok_or_else(|| aggregate_overflow(maintain))?;
            }
        }
        for (_, (key, change)) in totals {
            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, Some(true))?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn live_sum(&self, maintain: &Maintain) -> bool {
        matches!(maintain.kind, MaintainKind::Sum { .. }) && self.schema.table(&maintain.source).is_some_and(|source| source.is_expiring())
    }

    /// A zero sum is still a group while source rows remain: one signed
    /// contribution may expire before the other. Keep its candidate row so
    /// a scan, snapshot and offline replica can discover the later live sum.
    fn aggregate_source_present(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        // One returned source image and its encoded key (MemoryRows also materializes count_prefix).
        let bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.source]).saturating_mul(2);
        self.maintain_scratch(bytes, |runner| {
            let source = &runner.schema.tables[&maintain.source];
            let index = maintain.contribution_index();
            if !source.indexes.contains_key(&index) { return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("maintain {} needs its contribution index", maintain.target))); }
            runner.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
            let present = runner.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.count_prefix(allowance, &maintain.source, &index, key, 1))? != 0;
            // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — a local positive witness keeps zero; absence needs complete, currently held source coverage.
            if !present && runner.device && !runner.aggregate_source_complete(maintain, key)? {
                runner.unknown_fact(&maintain.source, &index, key, "zero-sum occupancy");
                return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("the zero-sum group's source occupancy is not known locally; queued without a predicted row".into()));
            }
            Ok(present)
        })
    }

    fn aggregate_source_complete(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        let source = &self.schema.tables[&maintain.source];
        if source.sync.as_ref().is_none_or(|sync| sync.horizon.is_some()) || self.schema.maintain_subset_unknown(&maintain.target) { return Ok(false); }
        // The target has the same bare audience keys, but no source horizon.
        if !self.upsert_absence_proven(&maintain.target, "byGroup", &target_group_key(maintain, key))? { return Ok(false); }
        for (name, index) in &source.indexes {
            let values = index.columns().iter().map_while(|column| maintain.by.iter().position(|field| field == column).map(|n| key[n].clone())).collect::<Vec<_>>();
            if self.retained_group(&maintain.source, name, &values)? { return Ok(false); }
        }
        Ok(true)
    }

    fn apply_aggregate(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: Vec<Value>, change: i128, source_present: Option<bool>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        if self.schema.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.owns(&maintain.target)) {
            return Err(super::timeline::refusal("E_TIMELINE_OWNED", "timeline-owned tables cannot be aggregate targets; maintain a mapped application table instead"));
        }
        let id = maintained_id(&key);
        let target = self.schema.table(&maintain.target).expect("validated");
        self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
        let existing = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, &maintain.target, &id))?;
        let target_key = target_group_key(maintain, &key);
        if self.device && existing.is_none() && !self.upsert_absence_proven(&maintain.target, "byGroup", &target_key)? {
            self.unknown_fact(&maintain.target, "byGroup", &target_key, "aggregate base");
            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("the affected aggregate value or its absence is not known locally; queued without a predicted row".into()));
        }
        let old_value = existing.as_ref().and_then(|row| row.field("value").ok()).map(Value::as_int).transpose()?.unwrap_or(0);
        let next = i128::from(old_value) + change;
        if !(I53_MIN as i128..=I53_MAX as i128).contains(&next) {
            return Err(aggregate_overflow(maintain));
        }
        let keep_zero = next == 0 && self.live_sum(maintain) && match source_present {
            Some(present) => present,
            None => self.aggregate_source_present(maintain, &key)?,
        };
        if next == 0 && !keep_zero {
            if let Some(existing) = existing {
                self.refuse_timeline_write(&maintain.target, crate::schema::Effect::Delete)?;
                let entries = self.tx.delete(&maintain.target, target, &existing)?;
                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
                self.row_changed(&maintain.target, Some(&existing), None, Origin::Maintained)?;
            }
            self.mirror_column(maintain, &key, 0)?;
            return Ok(());
        }
        let mut row = crate::small_map::collect([("id".to_owned(), Value::Id(id.clone())), ("value".to_owned(), Value::Int(next as i64))]);
        for (field, value) in maintain.group_fields().iter().zip(key.iter().cloned()) {
            row.insert(field.clone(), value);
        }
        // @ref LLP 3000.013.001#3-global-maintained-view-representation — stores index the one logical empty group by a hidden constant.
        if maintain.by.is_empty() { row.insert(GLOBAL.into(), Value::Bool(true)); }
        let row = Value::Row(row.into());
        if existing.as_ref() == Some(&row) { return Ok(()); }
        let entries = self.tx.put(&maintain.target, target, &row, existing.as_ref())?;
        self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
        self.row_changed(&maintain.target, existing.as_ref(), Some(&row), Origin::Maintained)?;
        self.mirror_column(maintain, &key, next as i64)
    }
}

pub(super) fn delta(maintain: &Maintain, source: &Value, direction: i64) -> Result<i128, RuntimeError> {
    Ok(match &maintain.kind {
        MaintainKind::Count => i128::from(direction),
        MaintainKind::Sum { of } => i128::from(direction).checked_mul(i128::from(source.field(of)?.as_int()?)).ok_or_else(|| aggregate_overflow(maintain))?,
    })
}

// @ref LLP 3000.007#17 — an internal sum names its maintain and column, never a retained contribution or computed value.
pub(super) fn aggregate_overflow(maintain: &Maintain) -> RuntimeError {
    RuntimeError::AggregateOverflow { maintain: maintain.private.as_ref().map_or_else(|| maintain.target.clone(), |o|o.table.clone()), column: maintain.private.as_ref().map_or_else(|| "value".into(), |o|o.column.clone()) }
}

#[cfg(all(test, feature = "sqlite"))]
mod timeline_tests {
    use super::*;
    #[test]
    fn timeline_owned_tables_cannot_be_maintain_targets() {
        let schema = crate::engine::timeline_authority::write_tests::schema();
        let mut store = crate::Store::memory().unwrap(); store.install(&schema).unwrap();
        let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        let mut runner = Runner::new(&tx, &schema, crate::Context::system().at(1), crate::meter::Meter::new(crate::Ceilings::unbounded(),crate::meter::Cut::Abort),0);
        let mut guard = runner.timeline_scope(crate::engine::timeline_authority::Authority::Transition("feed".into()));
        for suffix in crate::schema::timeline::OWNED_SUFFIXES {
            let maintain = Maintain { own_keys: None, row_key: None, parent_key: None, aliases: Default::default(), target: format!("feed{suffix}"), source: "follows".into(), by: vec!["readerId".into()],
                kind: MaintainKind::Count, filter: None, computed: Default::default(), residency: Default::default(), readable: None, private: None };
            let result = guard.apply_aggregate(&maintain, vec![Value::Id("reader".into())], 1, None);
            assert_eq!(result.unwrap_err().code(), "E_TIMELINE_OWNED");
        }
    }
}

//! Server activation builder; all fallible work precedes commit.
use super::*;
impl Engine {
    pub(super) fn activate(
        store: &mut Store,
        schema: &Schema,
        programs: &BTreeMap<String, Program>,
        release: Option<&release::ReleaseActivation>,
        now: i64,
        allow_feed_adoption: bool,
        expected_release: Option<u64>,
        expected_backend: Option<&crate::store::opening::Backend>,
    ) -> Result<(u64, crate::store::opening::Metadata), RuntimeError> {
        schema.validate_column_owners()?;

            crate::schema::ephemeral::admit_program(schema, program)?;

            for table in crate::ir::read_sites(program)
                .into_iter()
                .map(|s| s.table)

                schema.refuse_private(&table)?;

        for schedule in &schema.schedules {

                    "schedule {} has an invalid period or offset",
                    schedule.name

                return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!(
                    "schedule {} names missing job or action {}; restore or remove the schedule",
                    schedule.name, schedule.target

            };
            if program.kind == ProgramKind::Action {
                let seat = schedule
                    .service
                    .as_deref()
                    .filter(|seat| crate::identity::is_service(seat))
                    .ok_or_else(|| {
                        RuntimeError::Schema(
                            "a scheduled action requires its declared service seat".into(),
                        )
                    })?;
                actions::authorize(program, seat)?;
            } else if schedule.service.is_some() {
                return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(
                    "a scheduled job cannot name a service seat".into(),
                ));
            }
            if program.args.iter().any(|(name, kind)| {
                !matches!(name.as_str(), "periodStart" | "periodEnd")
                    || *kind != crate::ir::ArgType::Time
            }) {
                return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(
                    "scheduled work takes periodStart: time and periodEnd: time, or nothing".into(),
                ));
            }
        }
        let prior_items = std::cell::RefCell::new(Vec::new());
        let population=std::cell::Cell::new(None);
        let outcome=store.activate_at_with_launch(schema, Some(programs), false, now, allow_feed_adoption, |conn| {
            Store::check_selected_release(conn, expected_release)?;
            if let Some(backend) = expected_backend { backend.check(conn)?; }
            if let Some(options)=release {
                options.check(conn)?;

                conn.execute("INSERT INTO _meta(key,value) VALUES('activation_restore',?1) ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value=excluded.value",[if options.restore_dormant {"true"}else{"false"}])?;
            }
            Ok(())
        }, |tx, changed, report| {
            if let Some(options)=release {tx.set_meta("release",&options.release.to_string())?;}
            use rusqlite::OptionalExtension;
            let repair_live_sums = tx.conn().query_row("SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key = 'live_sum_candidates'", [], |row| row.get::<_, String>(0)).optional()?.as_deref() != Some("1");
            let previous: Option<String> = tx.conn().query_row("SELECT schema FROM _generations WHERE generation = (SELECT CAST(value AS INTEGER) FROM _meta WHERE key = 'generation')", [], |row| row.get(0)).optional()?;
            let previous: Option<Schema> = previous.map(|text| serde_json::from_str(&text).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::decode(e, RuntimeError::Store))).transpose()?;
            let needs_maintained_id_marker = (schema.maintains.iter().any(|maintain| maintain.row_key.is_none())

                // A newly introduced aggregate has no legacy identity map to
                // preserve. Keep its event-free recorded-path rebuild out of
                // commit accounting, as activation did before the address
                // migration existed.
                if !repair_maintained_ids {
                    capture.rebuild_recorded_activation(previous.as_ref(), &rebuild.iter().copied().filter(|m| m.private.is_none()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), report)?;
                }
            }
            let mut runner = Runner::new(tx, schema, Context::system().at(now), Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort), seq);
            if repair_maintained_ids {
                let started = std::time::Instant::now();
                let rewritten = runner.rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(&rebuild.iter().copied().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>(), previous.as_ref(), Some(tx))?;
                if rewritten != 0 { report.changes.push(format!("rewrote {rewritten} legacy aggregate references")); }
                report.detail("rewrite legacy aggregate references", started);
            }
            // Legacy maps must be captured before any activation rebuild can
            // remove their target rows. Recorded values themselves are
            // stamped first so their historical paths may still traverse the
            // predecessor addresses.
            if attribution && repair_maintained_ids {
                runner.rebuild_recorded_activation(previous.as_ref(), &rebuild.iter().copied().filter(|m| m.private.is_none()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), report)?;
            }
            runner.activate_columns(previous.as_ref(), &rebuild, &columns, Some(report))?;
            for maintain in rebuild.into_iter().filter(|m| m.private.is_none()) {
                if !recorded::table_paths_changed(schema.table(&maintain.source), previous.as_ref().and_then(|s| s.table(&maintain.source))) {
                    runner.rebuild_maintain_reported(maintain, report)?;
                }
            }
            let events = runner.events.take();
            let tables: Vec<String> = runner.written_tables.iter().cloned().collect();
            let written = runner.rows_written;
            drop(runner);
            if written > 0 || !columns.is_empty() {
                tx.record_commit(seq, now, "rebuild", crate::SYSTEM_PRINCIPAL, "rebuild", &tables, written)?;

        }, |tx| {
            if let Some(options)=release {
                crate::store::release_history::finalize_restorations(tx)?;
                let mut items=crate::store::release_history::inventory(tx.conn(),None,usize::MAX)?;
                let dormant_items=items.len();

                for item in &mut items {

                    let count=before.as_ref().map_or(0,|i|i.rows);
                    item.before_rows=Some(count);item.after_rows=Some(item.rows);

                    let restored=if item.kind=="rows" {

                    } else if item.kind=="column" {tx.meta(&format!("activation_column_restored:{}",item.path))?.and_then(|s|s.parse::<u64>().ok()).unwrap_or(0)} else {0};

        }

//! Referential actions on delete (LLP 3000.039 §3): before a delete removes
//! its row, reserve a schema-fixed charge, close over the `cascade`
//! references, refuse while a `restrict` reference still holds a closure row
//! from outside the closure, clear `set null` references outside it, and
//! remove the closure children first. The caller then removes the row itself.
// @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — closure first; probes exclude the closure; deletion dominates set null.
use crate::engine::runner::Runner;
use crate::{
    error::{MeterKind, RuntimeError},
    meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter},
    rows::{Bounds, Dir},
    schema::{Effect, references::{OnDelete, Referencing}},
    value::Value,
};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

impl Runner<'_> {
    pub(super) fn apply_reference_actions(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let schema = self.schema;
        if !schema.is_referenced(table_name) { return Ok(()); }
        let Some(price) = schema.delete_reservation(table_name) else {
            // A device without a reached child's exported price cannot charge
            // what the server charges; the server always has every price.
            if self.device { return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("deleting {table_name} needs every referencing table's write price; queued without a local delete"))); }
            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{table_name}'s delete actions have no reservation: a cascading reference lacks its cap or its child's write price (guide writes)")));
        };
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#4.2 — what the commit publishes is fixed by the schema, not by the rows the actions reach.
        let closure = schema.action_tables(table_name);
        // A public device projection carries the private column's price but
        // not the maintain that computes its value. If an action can write
        // such a source, settlement must supply the authoritative mirror.
        // @ref LLP 3000.007.001#3.7 — devices store maintained columns but never derive them.
        if self.device && closure.written.iter().any(|source| schema.write_reservation(source)
            .is_some_and(|plan| plan.price(crate::schema::reservations::COLUMNS)[3] != 0)) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("deleting {table_name} can change a server-maintained column; queued without a local delete")));
        }
        for table in &closure.written {
            if schema.visible(table) { self.written_tables.insert(table.clone()); }
            self.action_tables.insert(table.clone());
        }
        for table in &closure.read { self.read_tables.insert(table.clone()); }
        if !closure.written.is_empty() { self.tx.widen_change_evidence(); }
        for (kind, amount) in [(MeterKind::Steps, price[0]), (MeterKind::IndexEntries, price[1]), (MeterKind::Examined, price[2]), (MeterKind::RowsWritten, price[3]), (MeterKind::OutputBytes, price[5]), (MeterKind::RuleProbes, price[6])] {
            if amount > 0 { self.meter.charge(kind, amount)?; }
        }
        // Pending event images survive the closure and subsequent statements.
        // Keep their schema-fixed reservation until the request ends.
        let events = schema.delete_event_heap(table_name).unwrap_or(0);
        self.meter.heap(events)?;
        let mark = self.meter.mark();
        self.meter.heap(price[4].saturating_sub(events))?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — draw the reservation's rows from the request's physical allowance before the first seek.
        if !self.context.is_system() { self.tx.draw(table_name, price[2])?; }
        let meter = std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort));
        // The fixed action reservation prepays the closure itself, but held-
        // group and authority proofs remain device-only bounded work. Keep the
        // active allowance reachable by nested `device_work` calls while the
        // closure runs under its prepaid unbounded meter. Recursive cascade
        // removals see the already-stored allowance and must not take it over.
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.4 — every device-only proof spends the separate bounded physical-work allowance.
        let owns_device_allowance = self.device_work_active && self.device_allowance.is_none();
        let mut meter = Some(meter);
        if owns_device_allowance { self.device_allowance = meter.take(); }
        let prepaid = self.tx.reference_prepaid(true);
        let action = std::mem::replace(&mut self.engine_action, true);
        let result = self.reference_closure(table_name, old);
        self.engine_action = action;
        self.tx.reference_prepaid(prepaid);
        self.meter = if owns_device_allowance {
            self.device_allowance.take().expect("active device allowance")
        } else {
            meter.expect("prepaid action meter")
        };
        self.meter.release_heap(mark);
        result
    }

    /// Steps 3–6. The walk holds identities, never images: each child scan
    /// streams `PAGE` rows per seek, and every write rereads its row current.
    fn reference_closure(&mut self, root_table: &str, root: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let schema = self.schema;
        let mut seen: BTreeSet<(String, String)> = BTreeSet::from([(root_table.to_owned(), root.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned())]);
        // (Vectors, not maps: the web device pays for every new collection type.)
        let mut visits: Vec<(String, Value)> = vec![(root_table.to_owned(), root.field("id")?.clone())];
        // 3. Close over cascades, breadth first. Every reached row's referencing groups must be held on a device.
        let mut next = 0;
        while next < visits.len() {
            let (table, id) = visits[next].clone();
            next += 1;
            for r in schema.referencing(&table) {
                if self.device && !through_reference(&r) { self.prove_reference_held(&r, &id)?; }
                if r.action != OnDelete::Cascade { continue; }
                self.each_child(&r, &id, true, &mut |_, child| {
                    if seen.insert((r.child.to_owned(), child.as_str()?.to_owned())) { visits.push((r.child.to_owned(), child)); }
                    Ok(true)
                })?;
            }
        }
        // 4. Restrict: every probe runs, streaming past closure rows (the root
        // included) to the first outside witness; the first occupied reference
        // in schema order is reported. One reference's probes visit each closure
        // row at most once, plus one witness per probe (LLP 3000.039 §5.1).
        let mut occupied: Option<(String, String, String)> = None;
        for (table, id) in &visits {
            for r in schema.referencing(table) {
                if r.action != OnDelete::Restrict || through_reference(&r) { continue; }
                let mut outside = false;
                self.each_child(&r, id, false, &mut |_, child| {
                    outside = !seen.contains(&(r.child.to_owned(), child.as_str()?.to_owned()));
                    Ok(!outside)
                })?;
                let candidate = (r.child.to_owned(), r.column.to_owned(), table.clone());
                if outside && occupied.as_ref().is_none_or(|o| candidate < *o) { occupied = Some(candidate); }
            }
        }
        if let Some((child, column, parent)) = occupied {
            #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
            self.refusing_clause(&child, &format!("{column}: {parent} (on delete restrict)"));
            let via = if parent == root_table { String::new() } else { format!(", through a {parent} row this delete cascades to") };
            return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_REFERENCED", message: format!("{root_table} at {} is still referenced through {child}.{column} (on delete restrict){via}; delete or retarget those rows first, or declare the reference's action (guide writes)", self.statement_site) });
        }
        // A cascaded row can itself have a physically retained read-through
        // child. Decide that blocker before set-null writes begin, so expiry
        // can retain this root and continue without relying on transaction
        // rollback to undo a partial closure.
        for (table, id) in visits.iter().skip(1) {
            if self.physical_children_outside(table, id, &seen)? {
                return Err(self.parent_has_children(table));
            }
        }
        // 5. Set null outside the closure. Each group is gathered whole before
        // any of it is cleared: a clear can recount a sibling that shares the
        // reference's index and move it behind a page cursor. Each row is then
        // reread current before its write.
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — gather, then clear: no row moves out of a walk it has not finished.
        for (table, id) in &visits {
            for r in schema.referencing(table) {
                if r.action != OnDelete::SetNull { continue; }
                let mut group: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
                self.each_child(&r, id, true, &mut |_, child| {
                    let child = child.as_str()?.to_owned();
                    if !seen.contains(&(r.child.to_owned(), child.clone())) { group.push(child); }
                    Ok(true)
                })?;
                for child in group {
                    let current = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, r.child, &child))?;
                    if let Some(current) = current.filter(|row| row.field(r.column).is_ok_and(|v| v == id)) {
                        self.clear_reference(r.child, r.column, current)?;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        // 6. Delete the closure, children first, each from its current image.
        let reached: Vec<(String, String)> = visits[1..].iter().map(|(t, id)| Ok((t.clone(), id.as_str()?.to_owned()))).collect::<Result<_, RuntimeError>>()?;
        drop(visits);
        for (table, id) in deletion_order(schema, &reached) {
            let current = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, &table, &id))?;
            let Some(current) = current else { continue };
            self.delete_reached(&table, current)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Streams the ids of the live rows referencing `id` through `r` to
    /// `visit`, through its index, until `visit` answers false. A capped walk
    /// (cascade, set null) reads `PAGE` rows per seek and holds at most the
    /// reference's cap; a restrict probe reads one row per seek, so it examines
    /// nothing past its witness. Images are dropped before `visit` runs. Seeks
    /// start at the live suffix, so an expired backlog is never visited.
    fn each_child(&mut self, r: &Referencing<'_>, id: &Value, capped: bool, visit: &mut dyn FnMut(&mut Self, Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let schema = self.schema;
        let index = schema.reference_index(r.child, r.column).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{}.{} has no reference index", r.child, r.column)))?.to_owned();
        let (cap, page_rows) = if capped { (schema.reference_cap(r.child, r.column).map_or(u64::MAX, u64::from), PAGE) } else { (u64::MAX, 1) };
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#2.3 — seek on the effective deadline (a read-through child's `$deadline`), so no expired row is visited.
        let ranges = if r.table.expiry_column().is_some() && !through_reference(r) {
            let now = self.context.now.ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("delete clock is not pinned".into()))?;
            vec![(vec![id.clone(), Value::Null], None), (vec![id.clone()], Some(Value::Int(now)))]
        } else {
            vec![(vec![id.clone()], None)]
        };
        let mut live = 0_u64;
        for (prefix, gt) in ranges {
            let mut bounds = Bounds { gt, ..Default::default() };
            loop {
                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, r.child, &index, &prefix, &bounds, Dir::Asc, page_rows))?;
                let more = page.len() == page_rows;
                if let Some((_, key)) = page.last() { bounds.after = crate::key::decode(key).map(|v| v.into_iter().skip(prefix.len()).collect()); }
                let mut ids = Vec::with_capacity(page.len());
                for (row, _) in page {
                    if self.device {
                        // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.4 — a device predicts only over current rows: retained history queues the delete, and only a live, current (or own provisional) row is a witness.
                        // A retained, no longer current row is work the reservation does not
                        // price and a witness the device cannot judge: the delete queues.
                        if self.tx.retained_row(r.child, &row)? && !self.tx.current_row(r.child, &row)? {
                            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("deleting meets retained {} history that references it; queued without a local delete", r.child)));
                        }
                        if self.expired(r.table, &row) || !(self.tx.current_row(r.child, &row)? || self.is_provisional(r.child, &row)?) {
                            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("deleting needs a current image of every {} row that references it; queued without a local delete", r.child)));
                        }
                    } else if self.expired(r.table, &row) { continue; }
                    live += 1;
                    // Activation validates caps and every write keeps them; more than the cap
                    // is a store that broke its own invariant, never a hidden-row count.
                    if live > cap { return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{}.{} holds more rows than its cap for one {} row", r.child, r.column, r.column))); }
                    ids.push(row.field("id")?.clone());
                }
                for child in ids {
                    if !visit(self, child)? { return Ok(()); }
                }
                if !more { break; }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// A device predicts only over a referencing group it holds completely.
    // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.4 — the held-group proof of LLP 3000.007 §20.5, per closure row and reference.
    fn prove_reference_held(&mut self, r: &Referencing<'_>, id: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let index = self.schema.reference_index(r.child, r.column).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{}.{} has no reference index", r.child, r.column)))?.to_owned();
        let (child, key) = (r.child.to_owned(), [id.clone()]);
        // Key-decided readability, and the group itself held (a rejoined or
        // unacquired range is unknown even when the rule admits the viewer).
        if self.device_work(|runner| runner.upsert_absence_proven(&child, &index, &key))? && self.tx.current_group(&child, &index, &key)? { return Ok(()); }
        Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("deleting needs every {} row that references it held; queued without a local delete", r.child)))
    }

    /// The engine's own write of a `set null` reference: no rule, every constraint.
    fn clear_reference(&mut self, table: &str, column: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let mut new = old.clone();
        if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut new { fields.insert(column.to_owned(), Value::Null); }
        let patch = crate::value::object([(column, Value::Null)]);
        let outer = std::mem::replace(&mut self.engine_action, true);
        let result = self.target_attempt(table, |runner| {
            runner.reserve_maintains(table, &runner.schema.tables[table])?;
            runner.replace_authorized(table, old, new, true, &patch, 0)
        });
        self.engine_action = outer;
        result
    }

    /// The engine's own delete of a closure row: no rule, its constraints, its
    /// `read through` children's probe, maintains and partition events.
    fn delete_reached(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| {
            runner.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Delete)?;
            let table = &runner.schema.tables[table_name];
            runner.reserve_maintains(table_name, table)?;
            runner.delete_row(table_name, old)
        })
    }
}

/// Rows a child scan holds per seek: the reservation's transient `4 × row`
/// (LLP 3000.039 §5.1, `Schema::delete_reservation`).
const PAGE: usize = crate::schema::references::REFERENCE_PAGE;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::{Context, rows::{MemoryRows, Rows}, value::{Value, object}};

    #[test]
    fn prepaid_actions_keep_nested_device_proofs_bounded() {
        let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("nested-allowance.q".into(), r#"
table parents:
  public
table children:
  parent: parents on delete cascade
  cap 1 by parent
  public
"#.into())]);
        assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
        let schema: crate::Schema = crate::json_codec::from_text(
            &crate::json_codec::to_text(&bound.schema).unwrap(),
        ).unwrap();
        let rows = MemoryRows::new();
        let parent = object([("id", Value::Id("p".into()))]);
        rows.put("parents", &schema.tables["parents"], &parent, None).unwrap();
        rows.put("children", &schema.tables["children"], &object([
            ("id", Value::Id("c".into())), ("parent", Value::Id("p".into())),
        ]), None).unwrap();
        let price = schema.delete_reservation("parents").unwrap();
        let ceilings = Ceilings {
            steps: price[0], index_entries: price[1], examined: price[2],
            rows_written: price[3], heap_bytes: price[4], output_bytes: price[5],
            rule_probes: price[6],
        };
        let mut runner = Runner::new(&rows, &schema, Context::system().at(1), Meter::new(ceilings, Cut::Abort), 0);
        runner.device = true;
        // Model the commit-end walk after its outer device_work swap: the
        // bounded allowance is the active meter and no spare copy exists.
        runner.device_work_active = true;
        let error = runner.apply_reference_actions("parents", &parent).unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(&error, RuntimeError::Prediction(message) if message.contains("allowance exhausted")), "{error:?}");
        assert_eq!(runner.meter.used.steps, price[0] + 1, "the nested proof attempted its bounded step");
    }
}

fn through_reference(r: &Referencing<'_>) -> bool {
    r.table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.reference == r.column)
}

/// The closure's rows, children before parents: a table goes first when no
/// other reached table must be removed before it (the cascade and `read
/// through` edges are acyclic by `check`), and within a table, later
/// discoveries first.
fn deletion_order(schema: &crate::schema::Schema, reached: &[(String, String)]) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    let tables: Vec<&str> = {
        let mut seen = Vec::new();
        for (table, _) in reached { if !seen.contains(&table.as_str()) { seen.push(table.as_str()); } }
        seen
    };
    // edges: child table -> the reached tables it must be removed before
    // (its cascade parents and its `read through` parent; LLP 3000.039 §3).
    let mut edges: Vec<(&str, &str)> = Vec::new();
    for &child in &tables {
        for &parent in &tables {
            if child != parent && schema.deletion_precedes(child, parent) { edges.push((child, parent)); }
        }
    }
    let mut order: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
    let mut remaining = tables.clone();
    while !remaining.is_empty() {
        // A table no remaining table references can go now (its referencers are gone).
        let position = remaining.iter().position(|t| !remaining.iter().any(|other| other != t && edges.contains(&(*other, *t))))
            .unwrap_or(remaining.len() - 1);
        order.push(remaining.remove(position));
    }
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(reached.len());
    for table in order {
        out.extend(reached.iter().rev().filter(|(t, _)| t == table).cloned());
    }
    out
}

 succeeded in 0ms:
//! The device: the partition held in a store the host brings, the stream
//! applied a page at a time with the watermark, the outbox in submission
//! order beneath predictions kept over confirmed images, queries and
//! predictions through `engine::local`. One implementation, over
//! `DeviceStore` — SQLite on a native host, memory on the web — so the
//! language is bound once and every host answers alike (LLP 3000 §7).

use crate::store::{DeviceStore, DeviceTx};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use snapback4_core::engine::local;
use snapback4_core::error::{Refusal, RuntimeError};
use snapback4_core::ir::Program;
use snapback4_core::meter::Ceilings;
use snapback4_core::rows::{Bounds, Dir, Rows};
use snapback4_core::schema::{Audience, Index, LeavePolicy, Schema, Table, timeline::check_version};
use snapback4_core::value::Value;
use snapback4_core::{Context, QueryOutcome, wire};
use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

mod predictions; #[cfg(feature = "native")] mod opening_native;
#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
mod witness;
mod delivery;
mod deferred;
mod media;
mod upload;
mod snapshot;
mod history;
mod read_scopes;
mod search;
mod recorded;
mod expiry_clock;
mod boundary;
mod store_identity;
pub use store_identity::StoreObservation;

/// The compiled backend, as `GET /schema` sends it.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize)]
pub struct Backend {
    pub generation: u64,
    pub schema: Schema,
    pub programs: Vec<Program>,
}

impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Backend {
    fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
        #[derive(Deserialize)]
        struct Wire { generation: u64, schema: Schema, programs: Vec<Program> }
        let Wire { generation, mut schema, programs } = Wire::deserialize(deserializer)?;
        for program in &programs {
            if program.kind == snapback4_core::ir::ProgramKind::Mutation
                && schema.prediction_reservation_refusal(program).is_some()
                && let Some(fact) = schema.operations.get_mut(&program.name) {
                fact.predicts = Some("never".into());
            }
        }
        Ok(Self { generation, schema, programs })
    }
}

impl Backend {
    fn require_current_semantics(&self) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        if self.schema.legacy_semantic_capabilities.is_empty() { return Ok(()); }
        Err(RuntimeError::Structural {
            code: "E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY",
            message: format!(
                "backend omitted required semantic capabilities {:?}; the server must adopt and republish it before a device can execute it",
                self.schema.legacy_semantic_capabilities
            ),
        })
    }
}

/// One transaction's stream request inputs. A response may apply only while
/// no other owner has started a mutation send after this capture.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize)]
pub struct SyncState {
    pub receipt_outcomes: bool,
    pub outbox_status: bool,
    pub acquired: bool,
    pub backend_required: bool,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub restore_refusal: Option<Refusal>,
    pub store_id: Option<String>,
    pub watermark: u64,
    pub generation: u64,
    pub pending_ids: Vec<String>,
    pub pending_through: u64,
    pub pending_complete: bool,
    pub pending_bound: u64,
    pub transfer_watermark: u64,
    /// Cut echoed by head-only observations, including an abandoned snapshot
    /// whose images remain restore evidence but cannot authorize continuation.
    pub restore_watermark: u64,
    /// Highest retained image head at request time, not at response time.
    pub restore_images_at: u64,
    /// Raw expected metadata for atomic installation after a schema request.
    pub adoption_capture: BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>,
    pub transfer_store_id: Option<String>,
    pub snapshot_catchup: bool,
    pub send_revision: u64,
}

/// One event of the stream or a snapshot, as `POST /sync` sends it.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct StreamEvent {
    pub table: String,
    pub kind: String,
    pub id: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub data: Option<serde_json::Value>,
}

/// One page of `POST /sync`.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct StreamPage {
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub preserved: Option<Vec<String>>,
    /// Pinned server time of this authoritative page; old transports may omit it.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub now: Option<i64>,
    /// Private restore cut captured separately from a restarted snapshot's
    /// request cursor. It validates head evidence, never acquisition progress.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub captured_restore_watermark: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub captured_restore_images_at: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub images_at: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub committed_above: BTreeMap<String, u64>,
    /// Local declaration captured by sync_state, echoed by the transport.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub pending_through: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub pending_complete: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub pending_bound: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub acquisitions: Vec<wire::Acquisition>,
    /// Local request watermark and persisted acquisition watermark at capture.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub requested_watermark: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub captured_watermark: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub store_id: Option<String>,
    /// Local receipt captured before transport, not server-supplied metadata.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub send_revision: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub stage_snapshot: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub snapshot_catchup: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub acknowledged: BTreeMap<String, u64>,
    /// Outcome qualification for the corresponding acknowledgement. Older
    /// servers sent sequences alone, including for refused mutations.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    pub sent: BTreeMap<String, u64>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub held: Option<wire::HeldGroups>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub joined: wire::HeldGroups,
    pub snapshot: bool,
    pub events: Vec<StreamEvent>,
    pub watermark: u64,
    pub more: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub next: Option<String>,
    /// The server echoes the cursor that selected this snapshot page.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub after: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub generation: Option<u64>,
}

/// A queued write: the device's submission order, the op, its arguments,
/// the ids it minted, and the rows it predicted (`table/id`).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Queued {
    /// Device-owned upload dependency and bytes, transferred with this outbox entry.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub upload: Option<serde_json::Value>,
    pub id: String,
    pub seq: u64,
    pub op: String,
    pub args: serde_json::Value,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub new_ids: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub predicted: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub viewer: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub now: i64,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub predictable: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub sent_seq: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub receipt_store: Option<ReceiptStore>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub observed_seq: Option<u64>,
    /// Presentation only: absent before dispatch, empty after dispatch starts,
    /// or the last retryable refusal's code. Never receipt/replay authority.
    // @ref LLP 3000.019#3.3 — pending status travels with durable outbox custody.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub dispatch: Option<String>,
}

/// A receipt binds only to an advertised incarnation. Missing outer or inner
/// identity is unbound until the first real identity; replacement binds known
/// legacy receipts before changing the store.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ReceiptStore {
    pub id: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub success_seq: Option<u64>,
}

/// What a prediction left behind.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize)]
pub struct Predicted {
    pub new_ids: Vec<String>,
    pub result: serde_json::Value,
    pub written: Vec<String>,
    pub read: Vec<String>,
    /// The rows written, `table/id`, to withdraw if the server refuses.
    pub predicted: Vec<String>,
}
