//! The generation barrier checks predecessor audiences before destructive projection.
// @ref LLP 3000.014#7-activation — pinned time, child scan, capture before validation, atomic publication.
use crate::{
    error::RuntimeError,
    rows::{Bounds, Dir, Rows},
    schema::{RuleExpr, Schema, Table, through::PARENT_DEADLINE},
    value::Value,
};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

const EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR: &str = "$expiry-table";

/// Rotate a sweep's table order after the last table that consumed a bounded
/// visit. Per-table row cursors alone can starve every later table when an
/// earlier table contains a permanently restricted due row.
pub(crate) fn resume_expiry_tables(
    mut tables: Vec<String>,
    cursors: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>,
) -> Vec<String> {
    let after = cursors
        .get(EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR)
        .and_then(|cursor| cursor.first())
        .and_then(|value| value.as_str().ok());
    if let Some(index) = after.and_then(|after| tables.iter().position(|table| table == after)) {
        let next = (index + 1) % tables.len().max(1);
        tables.rotate_left(next);
    }
    tables
}

pub(crate) fn mark_expiry_table(cursors: &mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>, table: &str) {
    cursors.insert(EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR.into(), vec![Value::String(table.into())]);
}

/// Only inherited batches need staging. Preserve the streaming path for
/// existing schemas, including large fixture imports.
pub(crate) fn ancestor_order<'a, I>(
    schema: &Schema,
    rows: I,
) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = (String, Value)> + 'a>
where
    I: IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>,
    I::IntoIter: 'a,
{
    if schema.tables.values().all(|t| t.through.is_none()) {
        return Box::new(rows.into_iter());
    }
    let order = schema.through_order();
    let mut rows: Vec<_> = rows.into_iter().collect();
    rows.sort_by_key(|(name, _)| order.iter().position(|n| n == name).unwrap_or(usize::MAX));
    Box::new(rows.into_iter())
}

fn refusal(name: &str, count: usize, reason: &str, samples: &[String]) -> RuntimeError {
    RuntimeError::Structural {
        code: "E_READ_THROUGH_ADOPT",
        message: format!(
            "{name}: {count} child rows cannot adopt read through: {reason}; sample ids/parent values [{}]; rewrite: reconcile the named audience fields and live parents in a bridge release, then `snapback4 deploy <dir> --restore-dormant` (guide rules)",
            samples.join(", ")
        ),
    }
}

fn sample(samples: &mut Vec<String>, row: &Value, reference: &str, parent: &str) {
    fn bounded(text: &str) -> &str {
        let mut end = text.len().min(256);
        while !text.is_char_boundary(end) {
            end -= 1;
        }
        &text[..end]
    }
    if samples.len() < 5 {
        let id = row
            .field("id")
            .ok()
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str().ok())
            .unwrap_or("<missing>");
        let value = row
            .field(reference)
            .ok()
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str().ok())
            .unwrap_or("<missing>");
        samples.push(format!(
            "{}: {reference} -> {parent}[{}]",
            bounded(id),
            bounded(value)
        ));
    }
}

fn rows(
    tx: &dyn Rows,
    name: &str,
    mut visit: impl FnMut(Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>,
) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
    loop {
        let page = tx.scan(name, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256)?;
        if page.is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        for (row, key) in page {
            bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
            visit(row)?;
        }
    }
}

fn correspondence(
    child: &RuleExpr,
    parent: &RuleExpr,
) -> Option<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>> {
    if child.is_uniformly_readable() && parent.is_uniformly_readable() {
        return Some(Default::default());
    }
    fn walk(
        a: &serde_json::Value,
        b: &serde_json::Value,
        map: &mut std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>,
    ) -> bool {
        use serde_json::Value::*;
        match (a, b) {
            (Object(a), Object(b)) if a.len() == b.len() => {
                if let (Some(String(a)), Some(String(b))) = (a.get("Field"), b.get("Field")) {
                    if map.get(a).is_some_and(|old| old != b)
                        || map.iter().any(|(old, v)| v == b && old != a)
                    {
                        return false;
                    }
                    map.insert(a.clone(), b.clone());
                    true
                } else {
                    a.iter()
                        .all(|(k, a)| b.get(k).is_some_and(|b| walk(a, b, map)))
                }
            }
            (Array(a), Array(b)) if a.len() == b.len() => {
                a.iter().zip(b).all(|(a, b)| walk(a, b, map))
            }
            _ => a == b,
        }
    }
    let mut map = Default::default();
    walk(
        &serde_json::to_value(child).ok()?,
        &serde_json::to_value(parent).ok()?,
        &mut map,
    )
    .then_some(map)
}

/// The retirement phase shared by activation and its read-only occupancy
/// preview. Selection and the predecessor deadline predicate live here once;
/// checking a candidate must not count a row this phase would remove.
pub(crate) struct Retirement<'a> {
    affected: Vec<(String, &'a Table)>,
    now: i64,
}

impl<'a> Retirement<'a> {
    pub(crate) fn new(next: &Schema, previous: &'a Schema, now: i64) -> Self {
        let affected = next
            .through_order()
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|name| {
                let next = &next.tables[&name];
                let old = previous.table(&name)?;
                Self::changes_lifetime(next,old).then_some((name, old))
            })
            .collect();
        Self { affected, now }
    }

    fn changes_lifetime(next:&Table,old:&Table) -> bool {
        next.through != old.through || next.through.is_some() && (next.expire != old.expire || next.expire.as_ref().is_some_and(|field|old.defaults.get(field)!=next.defaults.get(field)))
    }

    pub(crate) fn retires_image(next:&Table,old:&Table,row:&Value,now:i64) -> bool {
        (next.through!=old.through || next.expire!=old.expire || old.expire.as_ref().is_some_and(|field|old.defaults.get(field)!=next.defaults.get(field))) && old.expired(row,now)
    }

    pub(crate) fn affects(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.affected.iter().any(|(table, _)| table == name)
    }

    pub(crate) fn retires(&self, name: &str, row: &Value) -> bool {
        self.affected
            .iter()
            .find(|(table, _)| table == name)
            .is_some_and(|(_, old)| old.expired(row, self.now))
    }
}

/// Capture barrier for an authoritative adapter's uncommitted generation.
pub fn activate(
    tx: &dyn Rows,
    next: &Schema,
    previous: Option<&Schema>,
    now: i64,
) -> Result<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, u64>, RuntimeError> {
    activate_retained(tx, next, previous, now, &Default::default())
}

pub(crate) fn activate_retained(
    tx: &dyn Rows,
    next: &Schema,
    previous: Option<&Schema>,
    now: i64,
    retained: &std::collections::BTreeSet<String>,
) -> Result<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, u64>, RuntimeError> {
    let mut shortened = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    let Some(previous) = previous else {
        return Ok(shortened);
    };
    // Previous indexes and row images still exist. Every affected expired row
    // retires under its old deadline, before a new default or capture can revive it.
    let retirement = Retirement::new(next, previous, now);
    for (name, old) in retirement.affected.iter().rev() {
        rows(tx, name, |row| {
            if retirement.retires(name, &row) {
                tx.delete(name, old, &row)?;
            }
            Ok(())
        })?;
    }
    // Compare all predecessor images before any ancestor is recaptured.
    for (name, _) in &retirement.affected {
        let Some(t) = &next.tables[name].through else {
            continue;
        };
        let Some(old) = previous.table(name).filter(|t| t.through.is_none()) else {
            continue;
        };
        let parent = previous
            .table(&t.parent)
            .ok_or_else(|| refusal(name, 0, "the previous parent schema is absent", &[]))?;
        let map = correspondence(&old.rules.read, &parent.rules.read);
        let mut invalid = 0;
        let mut samples = Vec::new();
        rows(tx, name, |row| {
            // @ref LLP 3000.000.000#10-wave-10-release-lifecycle-amendment — historical capture restoration needs no audience recapture.
            if retained.contains(name) && row.field(PARENT_DEADLINE).is_ok() && t.fields.keys().all(|f|row.field(f).is_ok()) {return Ok(());}
            let Some(map) = &map else {
                invalid += 1;
                sample(&mut samples, &row, &t.reference, &t.parent);
                return Ok(());
            };
            let row = crate::schema::row_image(&row, old);
            let parent_row = row
                .field(&t.reference)
                .ok()
                .and_then(|id| id.as_str().ok())
                .map(|id| tx.get(&t.parent, id))
                .transpose()?
                .flatten();
            let matches = parent_row.as_ref().is_some_and(|image| {
                !parent.expired(image, now) && {
                    let image = crate::schema::row_image(image, parent);
                    map.iter()
                        .all(|(child, p)| row.field(child).ok() == image.field(p).ok())
                }
            });
            if !matches {
                invalid += 1;
                sample(&mut samples, &row, &t.reference, &t.parent);
            }
            Ok(())
        })?;
        if invalid > 0 {
            return Err(refusal(
                name,
                invalid,
                "missing, ambiguous or disagreeing predecessor audience correspondence",
                &samples,
            ));
        }
    }
    for name in next.through_order() {
        let table = &next.tables[&name];
        let Some(t) = &table.through else {
            continue;
        };
        let parent = &next.tables[&t.parent];
        let recapture = previous.table(&name).and_then(|t| t.through.as_ref()) != Some(t);
        let mut invalid = 0;
        let mut samples = Vec::new();
        rows(tx, &name, |old| {
            let mut row = old.clone();
            // @ref LLP 3000.000.000#2-retain-by-default — restored audience/deadline captures retain their original lifetime.
            let historical = retained.contains(&name) && old.field(PARENT_DEADLINE).is_ok();
            if recapture && (!historical || t.fields.keys().any(|field| old.field(field).is_err()))
            {
                let parent_row = old
                    .field(&t.reference)
                    .ok()
                    .and_then(|id| id.as_str().ok())
                    .map(|id| tx.get(&t.parent, id))
                    .transpose()?
                    .flatten();
                // @ref LLP 3000.014#7-activation — previous-schema expiry was retired before projection; a newly due deadline must propagate, not veto adoption.
                let Some(parent_row) = parent_row else {
                    invalid += 1;
                    sample(&mut samples, &old, &t.reference, &t.parent);
                    return Ok(());
                };
                if historical {
                    let mut fresh = row.clone();
                    super::through::stamp(parent, t, &parent_row, &mut fresh)?;
                    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut row {
                        for field in t.fields.keys().filter(|field| old.field(field).is_err()) {
                            fields.insert(field.clone(), fresh.field(field)?.clone());
                        }
                    }
                } else {
                    super::through::stamp(parent, t, &parent_row, &mut row)?;
                }
            }
            table.recompute_deadline(&mut row)?;
            let before = previous.table(&name).and_then(|table| table.deadline(&old));
            if table
                .deadline(&row)
                .is_some_and(|after| before.is_none_or(|before| after < before))
            {
                *shortened.entry(name.clone()).or_default() += 1;
            }
            tx.put(&name, table, &row, Some(&old))?;
            Ok(())
        })?;
        if invalid > 0 {
            return Err(refusal(&name, invalid, "missing parent", &samples));
        }
    }
    Ok(shortened)
}

/// Trusted restoration validates the existing immutable captures; it never stamps them.
pub fn validate_restore(tx: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema, now: i64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    for name in schema.through_order() {
        let table = &schema.tables[&name];
        let Some(t) = &table.through else {
            continue;
        };
        let parent = &schema.tables[&t.parent];
        let mut invalid = 0;
        let mut samples = Vec::new();
        rows(tx, &name, |row| {
            let found = row
                .field(&t.reference)
                .ok()
                .and_then(|v| v.as_str().ok())
                .map(|id| tx.get(&t.parent, id))
                .transpose()?
                .flatten();
            let matches = found.as_ref().is_some_and(|p| {
                (!parent.expired(p, now) || table.expired(&row, now)) && {
                    let p = crate::schema::row_image(p, parent);
                    t.fields
                        .iter()
                        .all(|(field, source)| row.field(field).ok() == p.field(source).ok())
                        && row.field(PARENT_DEADLINE).ok()
                            == Some(&parent.deadline(&p).map(Value::Int).unwrap_or(Value::Null))
                }
            });
            if !matches {
                invalid += 1;
                sample(&mut samples, &row, &t.reference, &t.parent);
            }
            Ok(())
        })?;
        if invalid > 0 {
            return Err(refusal(
                &name,
                invalid,
                "restored captures do not match a live parent",
                &samples,
            ));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub fn validate_indexes(tx: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    for (name, table) in &schema.tables {
        let mut checks: Vec<_> = table
            .indexes
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, i)| i.unique)
            .map(|(name, i)| (name, i.components.len(), 1, true))
            .collect();
        for constraint in &table.constraints {
            if let crate::schema::Constraint::Cap { by, max } = constraint {
                let (index, _) = table
                    .indexes
                    .iter()
                    .find(|(_, i)| i.columns().starts_with(by))
                    .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{name} cap has no index")))?;
                checks.push((index, by.len(), u64::from(*max), false));
            }
        }
        for (index, width, max, nulls_distinct) in checks {
            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
            let mut previous = None;
            let mut count = 0;
            loop {
                let page = tx.scan(name, index, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256)?;
                if page.is_empty() {
                    break;
                }
                for (_, key) in page {
                    let full = crate::key::decode(&key)
                        .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Store("invalid activation index".into()))?;
                    let group = full[..width].to_vec();
                    bounds.after = Some(full);
                    if nulls_distinct && group.contains(&Value::Null) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    if previous.as_ref() == Some(&group) {
                        count += 1;
                    } else {
                        previous = Some(group);
                        count = 1;
                    }
                    if count > max {
                        return Err(RuntimeError::Constraint(format!(
                            "cannot activate {name}.{index}: existing group exceeds {max}"
                        )));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

impl super::runner::Runner<'_> {
    /// Authoritative adapters feed an ancestor-ordered batch to the ordinary
    /// insert/update path; captures always resolve inside this transaction.
    pub fn seed_server_rows(
        &mut self,
        rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>,
    ) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
                "server seed requires system authority".into(),
            ));
        }
        let order = self.schema.through_order();
        let mut rows: Vec<_> = rows.into_iter().collect();
        rows.sort_by_key(|(n, _)| order.iter().position(|x| x == n));
        let count = rows.len() as u64;
        for (name, row) in rows {
            super::timeline::check_import(self.schema, &name)?;
            // Adoption rewrites are system imports of stored images (LLP 3000.015 §1).
            self.upsert(
                &name,
                &row.field("id")?.clone(),
                row.import_input(&super::ImportInput(())),
            )?;
        }
        self.check_final_exists()?;
        Ok(count)
    }

    /// A bounded child-first sweep on the common Rows interface.
    pub fn sweep_server_rows(&mut self, limit: usize, expiry_after: &mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
                "server sweep requires system authority".into(),
            ));
        }
        let now = self
            .context
            .now
            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("sweep clock is not pinned".into()))?;
        let mut count = 0;
        let mut visited = 0;
        let tables = resume_expiry_tables(self.schema.through_order().into_iter().rev().collect(), expiry_after);
        for name in tables {
            let Some((index, _)) = self.schema.tables[&name].expiry_index() else {
                continue;
            };
            let due = Bounds { gte: Some(Value::Int(i64::MIN)), lte: Some(Value::Int(now)), ..Default::default() };
            let mut bounds = due.clone();
            bounds.after = expiry_after.get(&name).cloned();
            let mut wrapped = bounds.after.is_none();
            while visited < limit {
                let batch = (limit - visited).min(256);
                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, scope| {
                    runner
                        .tx
                        .scan(scope, &name, index, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, batch)
                })?;
                if page.is_empty() {
                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
                        bounds = due.clone();
                        wrapped = true;
                        continue;
                    }
                    break;
                }
                let page_len = page.len();
                for (row, key) in page {
                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
                    if let Some(after) = &bounds.after { expiry_after.insert(name.clone(), after.clone()); }
                    visited += 1;
                    mark_expiry_table(expiry_after, &name);
                    match self.retire_expired_row(&name, &row) {
                        Ok(true) => count += 1,
                        Ok(false) => {},
                        Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_REFERENCED" | "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN", .. }) => {},
                        Err(error) => return Err(error),
                    }
                }
                if page_len < batch {
                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
                        bounds = due.clone();
                        wrapped = true;
                        continue;
                    }
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(count)
    }
}

//! Experimental Postgres backend for evaluating real Quarry execution.
//! Not a deploy target: no auth host, migrations, native module, asset ledger,
//! jobs, actions, or effect worker. Callers are trusted hosts, as with Engine.
//! @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — evaluate storage portability before productizing it
mod log;
mod store;
mod caps;
mod contribution_upgrade;
mod maintained_identity_upgrade;
mod authority;
mod prefetch;
mod tail;
mod through;
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;
pub use store::{SCAN_MEMORY_GUARD, WriteMode};

use super::{Context, MutationOutcome, QueryOutcome, WriteState, runner::Runner, validate};
use crate::{
    error::{Refusal, RuntimeError},
    ir::{ArgType, Program, ProgramKind},
    meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter, Metered},
    partition::{self, PartitionRows, SnapshotCursor, SnapshotPage, StreamPage},
    schema::Schema,
    value::{Value, canonical_json},
};
use postgres::{Client, error::SqlState};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use store::{Store, decode, namespace};
use crate::rows::Rows;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, serde::Serialize)]
pub struct Stats {
    /// Explicit driver calls including BEGIN/COMMIT and cold prepares, not a
    /// packet count. Implicit rollback when an errored transaction drops is omitted.
    pub database_calls: u64,
    pub transaction_retries: u64,
    pub prefetch_marked_reads: u64,
    /// Largest marked page in the most recent transaction.
    pub prefetch_page_reads: u64,
    pub prefetch_rows_transferred: u64,
    pub prefetch_bytes_transferred: u64,
}

pub struct PostgresEngine {
    store: Store,
    schema: Schema,
    programs: BTreeMap<String, Program>,
    ceilings: Ceilings,
    mode: WriteMode,
    retries: u64,
    precharge: Metered,
    expiry_after: BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>,
}

impl PostgresEngine {
    /// Create a NEW, isolated sb4_eval_* namespace; never replace an existing
    /// schema. TLS/credentials are owned by the caller's configured Client.
    pub fn create(
        client: Client,
        name: &str,
        mut schema: Schema,
        programs: impl IntoIterator<Item = Program>,
    ) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
        let name = namespace(name)?;
        refuse_maintained_columns(&schema)?;
        super::columns::validate_before_prepare(&schema)?;
        schema.prepare_contribution_indexes();
        let programs: BTreeMap<_, _> = programs.into_iter().map(|p| (p.name.clone(), p)).collect();
        supported(&schema, &programs)?;
        Self::attach(client, schema, programs, Some(&name))
    }

    /// Reopen the persisted compiled generation; subsequent transactions refuse
    /// if another connection activates a successor.
    pub fn open(mut client: Client, name: &str) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
        let name = namespace(name)?;
        client.batch_execute(&format!("SET search_path = {name}, pg_catalog;"))?;
        let row = client.query_one("SELECT version,schema,programs FROM _backend WHERE singleton", &[])?;
        if row.get::<_, &str>(0) != store::VERSION {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Store("not this Postgres evaluation store version".into()));
        }
        let schema = decode(row.get(1))?;
        let programs = decode(row.get(2))?;
        supported(&schema, &programs)?;
        // Existing immutable stores adopt this portable admission policy at open.
        // Return one offending index and its exact count, never its row payloads.
        if let Some(row) = client.query(
            "SELECT t, ix, COUNT(*) FROM i WHERE octet_length(k) > $1 GROUP BY t, ix ORDER BY t, ix LIMIT 1",
            &[&(crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES as i32)],
        )?.first() {
            return Err(crate::rows::index_key_refusal(row.get(0), row.get(1), row.get::<_, i64>(2) as u64));
        }
        Self::attach(client, schema, programs, None)
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.033#1.3 — read-session storage and all other upgrades
    // commit together, only after every open/adoption check has succeeded.
    fn attach(client: Client, mut schema: Schema, programs: BTreeMap<String, Program>, create: Option<&str>) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
        let mut store = Store::new(client);
        let tx = store.opening_transaction()?;
        tx.batch("SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '5s'; SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s';")?;
        if let Some(name) = create {
            tx.batch(&format!("CREATE SCHEMA {name}; SET search_path = {name}, pg_catalog;"))?;
            tx.batch(store::DDL)?;
            tx.execute("INSERT INTO _backend VALUES (true,$1,$2,$3)",
                &[&store::VERSION, &canonical_json(&schema), &canonical_json(&programs)])?;
        }
        tx.query("SELECT seq FROM _head WHERE singleton FOR UPDATE", &[])?;
        // Admission must use the backend that survived the wait for the head.
        // A format change can leave schema/program bytes unchanged.
        let held = tx.query("SELECT version,schema,programs FROM _backend WHERE singleton", &[])?.remove(0);
        if held.get::<_, &str>(0) != store::VERSION {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Store("not this Postgres evaluation store version".into()));
        }
        let held_schema: Schema = decode(held.get(1))?;
        let held_programs: BTreeMap<String, Program> = decode(held.get(2))?;
        supported(&held_schema, &held_programs)?;
        if held_schema.hash() != schema.hash() || canonical_json(&held_programs) != canonical_json(&programs) {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Generation("the backend changed while opening; reopen its current generation".into()));
        }
        // Even a no-op ALTER takes an exclusive table lock. Reopening an
        // upgraded store must remain possible while another reader holds it.
        for (column, ddl) in [
            ("generation", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN generation BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1"),
            ("through_shortened", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN through_shortened TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'"),
            ("maintained_identity_version", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN maintained_identity_version TEXT"),
        ] {
            let exists: bool = tx.query("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = '_backend'::regclass AND attname = $1 AND NOT attisdropped)", &[&column])?[0].get(0);
            if !exists { tx.batch(ddl)?; }
        }
        // Repeat admission under the head fence used by physical adoption.
        if let Some(row) = tx.query(
            "SELECT t, ix, COUNT(*) FROM i WHERE octet_length(k) > $1 GROUP BY t, ix ORDER BY t, ix LIMIT 1",
            &[&(crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES as i32)],
        )?.first() {
            return Err(crate::rows::index_key_refusal(row.get(0), row.get(1), row.get::<_, i64>(2) as u64));
        }
        tx.batch("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _sequences (parent TEXT NOT NULL, id TEXT NOT NULL, value BIGINT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(parent, id));")?;
        tx.batch(store::READ_SESSIONS_DDL)?;
        tx.batch("DROP INDEX IF EXISTS _log_row_seq; DROP INDEX IF EXISTS _log_row_seq_kind;")?;
        caps::install(&tx, &schema)?;
        let generation = contribution_upgrade::install(&tx, &mut schema)?;
        let generation = maintained_identity_upgrade::install(&tx, &schema, create.is_some(), generation)?;
        // Retain the adapter's ordinary connection limits on successful open.
        tx.batch("SET statement_timeout = '5s'; SET lock_timeout = '5s';")?;
        tx.commit()?;
        store.generation = generation;
        schema.prepare_delivery_lookup();
        Ok(Self { store, schema, programs, ceilings: Ceilings::default(), mode: WriteMode::Serialized, retries: 0, precharge: Metered::default(), expiry_after: BTreeMap::new() })
    }

    pub fn schema(&self) -> &Schema {
        &self.schema
    }
    pub fn programs(&self) -> &BTreeMap<String, Program> {
        &self.programs
    }
    pub fn generation(&self) -> u64 {
        self.store.generation
    }
    pub fn set_ceilings(&mut self, ceilings: Ceilings) {
        self.ceilings = ceilings;
    }
    pub fn set_write_mode(&mut self, mode: WriteMode) {
        self.mode = mode;
    }
    /// Evaluation switch: only physical access changes, never the runner.
    pub fn set_prefetch(&mut self, enabled: bool) { self.store.prefetch = enabled; }
    /// Differential evaluation: reserve budget before the first logical charge.
    pub fn set_meter_precharge(&mut self, used: Metered) { self.precharge = used; }

    pub fn stats(&self) -> Stats {
        Stats { database_calls: self.store.calls.get(), transaction_retries: self.retries,
            prefetch_marked_reads: self.store.marked_reads.get(), prefetch_page_reads: self.store.page_reads.get(), prefetch_rows_transferred: self.store.prefetch_rows.get(),
            prefetch_bytes_transferred: self.store.prefetch_bytes.get() }
    }

    pub fn query(&mut self, name: &str, context: Context) -> Result<QueryOutcome, Refusal> {
        self.query_with_delivery(name, context, super::DeliveryManifest::Build)
    }

    pub fn query_with_delivery(&mut self, name: &str, mut context: Context, manifest: super::DeliveryManifest) -> Result<QueryOutcome, Refusal> {
        context.generation = self.generation();
        let program = self.programs.get(name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::UnknownOp(name.into()))?;
        if program.kind != ProgramKind::Query {
            return Err(RuntimeError::UnknownOp(format!("{name} is not a query")).into());
        }
        super::server_query_allowed(&self.schema, name)?;
        validate::validate_inputs(&self.schema, program, &mut context.args)?;
        context.now.get_or_insert_with(crate::now_ms);
        let tx = self.store.transaction(None)?;
        let seq = tx.next_seq()? - 1;
        let mut runner = Runner::new(&tx, &self.schema, context, Meter::new(self.ceilings, Cut::Cap), seq);
        runner.meter.used = self.precharge;
        let data = runner.run(program)?;
        runner.charge_output(&data)?;
        let (delivery, delivery_meter) = match manifest { super::DeliveryManifest::Build => runner.delivery_manifest(&data), super::DeliveryManifest::Skip => (None, None) };
        let outcome = QueryOutcome { decoration_expiry: runner.decoration_expiry, search_rows: runner.search_rows.take(), search_scopes: None, delivery, delivery_meter, ephemeral: None,
            unavailable: runner.query_unavailable,
            complete: runner.meter.capped_at.is_none()
                && runner.word_cut_at.is_none()
                && !runner.non_uniform
                && !runner.page_overflow
                && !runner.value_source_incomplete
                && !runner.page_position_lost(),
            cut: runner.read_cut(),
            capped_at: runner.meter.capped_at.clone(),
            word_cut_at: runner.word_cut_at.clone(),
            next: runner.outcome_next_cursor()?,
            data,
            seq,
            metered: runner.meter.used,
            tables: runner.read_tables.iter().cloned().collect(),
            next_expiry: runner.next_expiry.get(),
        };
        drop(runner);
        tx.rollback()?;
        Ok(outcome)
    }

    pub fn replay(&mut self, viewer: &str, op: &str) -> Result<Option<MutationOutcome>, RuntimeError> {
        let tx = self.store.transaction(None)?;
        let receipt = tx.applied(viewer, op)?;
        tx.rollback()?;
        receipt.as_deref().map(MutationOutcome::from_receipt).transpose()
    }

    /// Compare wire identity before decoding against the installed program.
    // @ref LLP 3000.009#5.1 — an id binds the admitted operation and arguments.
    fn replay_mutation(&mut self, viewer: &str, id: &str, name: &str, args_digest: &str) -> Result<Option<MutationOutcome>, RuntimeError> {
        let tx = self.store.transaction(None)?;
        let receipt = tx.applied_bound(viewer, id, name, args_digest)?;
        tx.rollback()?;
        receipt.as_deref().map(MutationOutcome::from_receipt).transpose()
    }

    pub fn mutate(&mut self, name: &str, op: Option<&str>, mut context: Context) -> Result<MutationOutcome, RuntimeError> {
        context.generation = self.generation();
        let wire_args = if op.is_some() { context.wire_args.take().unwrap_or_else(|| serde_json::Value::Object(crate::wire::map_to_json(&context.args))) }
            else { serde_json::Value::Null };
        let args_digest = crate::store::payload_digest(&wire_args);
        // Preserve the bound replay-before-validation contract, including
        // unknown or renamed programs. Never return a historical result row.
        if let Some(op) = op
            && let Some(outcome) = self.replay_mutation(&context.viewer, op, name, &args_digest)?
        {
            return Ok(outcome);
        }
        let program = self.programs.get(name).ok_or_else(|| {
            self.schema.check_delivery(name, context.delivery_fingerprint.as_deref()).err()
                .unwrap_or_else(|| RuntimeError::UnknownOp(name.into()))
        })?.clone();
        context.now.get_or_insert_with(crate::now_ms);
        if context.entropy == 0 {
            context.entropy = crate::ids::seed();
        }
        // @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — retries rerun Quarry, rules, maintains, and bookkeeping together
        for attempt in 0..=32 {
            match self.mutate_once(&program, op, context.clone(), &args_digest) {
                Err(error) if retry_transaction(&error) && attempt < 32 => {
                    self.retries += 1;
                    let delay = (100_u64 << attempt.min(6)) + crate::ids::seed() % 250;
                    std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_micros(delay));
                }
                outcome => return outcome,
            }
        }
        unreachable!()
    }

    fn mutate_once(&mut self, program: &Program, op: Option<&str>, mut context: Context, args_digest: &str) -> Result<MutationOutcome, RuntimeError> {
        let tx = self.store.transaction(Some(self.mode))?;
        if let Some(op) = op
            && let Some(receipt) = tx.applied_bound(&context.viewer, op, &program.name, args_digest)?
        {
            let outcome = MutationOutcome::from_receipt(&receipt)?;
            tx.rollback()?;
            return Ok(outcome);
        }
        self.schema.check_delivery(&program.name, context.delivery_fingerprint.as_deref())?;
        if program.kind != ProgramKind::Mutation {
            return Err(RuntimeError::UnknownOp(format!("{} is not a mutation", program.name)));
        }
        if let Err(error) = validate::validate_inputs(&self.schema, program, &mut context.args) {
            return Ok(failed(error.refusal(), None, Metered::default()));
        }
        let viewer = context.viewer.clone();
        let now = context.now.unwrap_or(0);
        let seq = tx.next_seq()?;
        tx.batch("SAVEPOINT program")?;
        let mut runner = Runner::new(&tx, &self.schema, context, Meter::new(self.ceilings, Cut::Abort), seq);
        runner.meter.used = self.precharge;
        let ran = runner.run(program).and_then(|value| {
            runner.charge_output(&value)?;
            Ok(value)
        });
        let ran = ran.and_then(|value| runner.retire_expired_births().map(|_| value))
            .and_then(|value| runner.check_final_exists().map(|_| value));
        let metered = runner.meter.used;
        let tables: Vec<String> = runner.written_tables.iter().cloned().collect();
        let events = runner.events.take();
        let action_tables = std::mem::take(&mut runner.action_tables);
        let outbox = std::mem::take(&mut runner.outbox);
        let writes = runner.rows_written;
        drop(runner);
        let outcome = match ran {
            Ok(result) => {
                tx.batch("RELEASE SAVEPOINT program")?;
                // @ref LLP 3000.022#6 — same receipt-only transaction and committed watermark as SQLite.
                let receipt_only = writes == 0 && outbox.is_empty()
                    && self.schema.delivery.iter().any(|binding| binding.mutation == program.name);
                let seq = seq - u64::from(receipt_only);
                if !receipt_only {
                    tx.record_commit(seq, now, &program.name, &viewer, program.kind.word(), &tables, writes)?;
                    partition::append(&tx, seq, &events)?;
                    tx.record_effects(&outbox, seq, now)?;
                }
                MutationOutcome { receipt_only, state: WriteState::Sent { seq, result }, metered, tables, events: partition::disclosed_event_count(&self.schema, &events, &action_tables), replayed: false }
            }
            Err(error) if error.is_refusal() => {
                tx.rollback_program()?;
                let current = if let RuntimeError::Conflict { current } = &error {
                    let mut probe = Runner::new(
                        &tx,
                        &self.schema,
                        Context::new(&viewer, BTreeMap::new()).at(now),
                        Meter::new(Ceilings::default(), Cut::Cap),
                        0,
                    );
                    probe.get(current).ok()
                } else {
                    None
                };
                failed(error.refusal(), current, metered)
            }
            Err(error) => return Err(error), // dropping the transaction rolls back ALL state
        };
        if let Some(op) = op {
            let recorded_seq = match outcome.state {
                WriteState::Sent { seq, .. } => seq,
                WriteState::Failed { .. } => seq - 1,
            };
            tx.record_applied(&viewer, op, recorded_seq, &canonical_json(&outcome.receipt(Some(op))), &program.name, args_digest, now)?;
        }
        tx.commit()?;
        Ok(outcome)
    }

    /// Load rows exactly as given: validated and indexed, rules, constraints
    /// and aggregates skipped, partition events emitted. For fixtures whose
    /// aggregates are already computed and for the conformance corpus.
    pub fn load(&mut self, rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        if self.schema.tables.values().any(|t|t.through.is_some()) { return self.seed_at(rows,crate::now_ms()); }
        let now = crate::now_ms();
        let tx = self.store.transaction(Some(WriteMode::Serialized))?;
        let seq = tx.next_seq()?;
        let mut runner = Runner::new(&tx, &self.schema, Context::system().at(now), Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort), seq);
        let mut count = 0;
        for (table_name, row) in rows {
            let old = tx.get(&table_name, row.field("id")?.as_str()?)?;
            let row = runner.import_sequences(&table_name, row, old.as_ref(), false)?;
            validate::validate_row(&self.schema, &table_name, &row)?;
            let table = self.schema.table(&table_name).expect("validated").clone();
            let id = row.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
            let old = tx.get(&table_name, &id)?;
            tx.put(&table_name, &table, &row, old.as_ref())?;
            partition::row_changed(&mut runner, &table_name, old.as_ref(), Some(&row), crate::engine::write::Origin::Source)?;
            runner.written_tables.insert(table_name);
            count += 1;
        }
        let events = runner.events.take();
        let tables: Vec<String> = runner.written_tables.iter().cloned().collect();
        drop(runner);
        if count > 0 {
            tx.record_commit(seq, now, "load", crate::SYSTEM_PRINCIPAL, "load", &tables, count)?;
            partition::append(&tx, seq, &events)?;
        }
        tx.commit()?;
        Ok(count)
    }

    /// Fixture loading still uses the real validation, maintains and sync paths.
    pub fn seed_at(&mut self, rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>, now: i64) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        let rows = super::through_activation::ancestor_order(&self.schema,rows);
        let tx = self.store.transaction(Some(WriteMode::Serialized))?;
        let seq = tx.next_seq()?;
        let mut runner = Runner::new(&tx, &self.schema, Context::system().at(now), Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort), seq);
        let mut count = 0;
        for (table, row) in rows {
            runner.upsert(&table, &row.field("id")?.clone(), row.import_input(&crate::engine::ImportInput(())))?;
            count += 1;
        }
        let final_exists = runner.satisfied_final_exists()?;
        runner.retire_seeded_view_sources()?;
        runner.check_final_exists_witnesses(&final_exists)?;
        let events = runner.events.take();
        let tables: Vec<String> = runner.written_tables.iter().cloned().collect();
        drop(runner);
        if count > 0 {
            tx.record_commit(seq, now, "seed", crate::SYSTEM_PRINCIPAL, "seed", &tables, count)?;
            partition::append(&tx, seq, &events)?;
        }
        tx.commit()?;
        Ok(count)
    }

    pub fn snapshot_page(
        &mut self,
        viewer: &str,
        cursor: Option<SnapshotCursor>,
        limit: usize,
        now: i64,
    ) -> Result<SnapshotPage, RuntimeError> {
        let tx = self.store.transaction(None)?;
        let page = partition::snapshot_page(&tx, &self.schema, viewer, cursor, limit, now)?;
        tx.rollback()?;
        Ok(page)
    }

    pub fn stream(&mut self, viewer: &str, watermark: u64, limit: usize, now: i64) -> Result<StreamPage, RuntimeError> {
        let tx = self.store.transaction(None)?;
        let page = partition::stream(&tx, &self.schema, viewer, watermark, limit, now)?;
        tx.rollback()?;
        Ok(page)
    }
}

fn failed(why: Refusal, current: Option<Value>, metered: Metered) -> MutationOutcome {
    MutationOutcome { receipt_only: false, state: WriteState::Failed { why, current }, metered, tables: Vec::new(), events: 0, replayed: false }
}

fn retry_transaction(error: &RuntimeError) -> bool {
    let RuntimeError::Postgres(error) = error else {
        return false;
    };
    let Some(error) = error.as_db_error() else {
        return false;
    };
    error.code() == &SqlState::T_R_SERIALIZATION_FAILURE || error.code() == &SqlState::T_R_DEADLOCK_DETECTED
        // Two concurrent refused operations can race only on their receipt;
        // neither advances the commit head. Recheck that receipt from scratch.
        || (error.code() == &SqlState::UNIQUE_VIOLATION && error.constraint() == Some("_ops_pkey"))
}

fn supported(schema: &Schema, programs: &BTreeMap<String, Program>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    if schema.tables.values().any(|t| t.ephemeral.is_some()) {
        return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_QUARRY_EPHEMERAL", message: "Postgres evaluation does not support ephemeral tables; use the SQLite server".into() });
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.003#4-advancing-time-without-an-application-job — an adapter without the private ledger cannot serve timed rows.
    if schema.tables.values().any(|t| t.not_before.is_some()) {
        return Err(RuntimeError::Schema("Postgres evaluation does not implement timed-publication state; use the SQLite server for `not before` tables".into()));
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.000.000#9 — the evaluation adapter records no audience epoch; unions stay on SQLite.
    if schema.tables.values().any(|t| t.sync.as_ref().is_some_and(crate::schema::Sync::is_union)) {
        return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_SYNC", message: "Postgres evaluation does not support union sync audiences; use the SQLite server".into() });
    }
    refuse_maintained_columns(schema)?;
    schema.validate_column_owners()?;
    for program in programs.values() {
        for table in crate::ir::read_sites(program).into_iter().map(|s|s.table).chain(crate::ir::write_tables(program).into_iter().map(|(t,_)|t)) { schema.refuse_private(&table)?; }
    }
    if let Some(issue) = crate::schema::validate(schema).first() {
        return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{}: {}", issue.path, issue.message)));
    }
    fn asset_arg(arg: &ArgType) -> bool {
        match arg {
            ArgType::Image { .. } | ArgType::Video { .. } | ArgType::File { .. } => true,
            ArgType::Optional(inner) | ArgType::List { of: Some(inner), .. } | ArgType::ListRange { of: Some(inner), .. } => asset_arg(inner),
            _ => false,
        }
    }
    if !schema.schedules.is_empty() || !schema.routes.is_empty()
        || schema.tables.values().any(|t| t.columns.values().any(|c| c.contains_asset()))
        || programs
            .values()
            .any(|p| p.native || !matches!(p.kind, ProgramKind::Query | ProgramKind::Mutation) || p.args.values().any(asset_arg))
    {
        return Err(RuntimeError::Schema("Postgres evaluation supports data queries/mutations and transactional emit records only; assets, native modules, jobs, actions, routes and schedules are not implemented".into()));
    }
    Ok(())
}

// @ref LLP 3000.007.001#3.11 — this evaluation backend claims no maintained-column parity.
fn refuse_maintained_columns(schema: &Schema) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    if schema.maintains.iter().any(|m|m.row_key.is_some()) {return Err(RuntimeError::Structural {code:"E_VIEW_KEY",message:"Postgres evaluation has no background recount runner; use the SQLite engine for row-keyed views (guide maintains)".into()});}
    if schema.tables.iter().all(|(name,table)| table.maintained.keys().all(|field|
        schema.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.private.as_ref().is_some_and(|o| &o.table == name && &o.column == field)
            && schema.table(&m.source).is_some_and(|s| !s.is_expiring() && s.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| &t.parent == name && m.by == [t.reference.clone()])))))
        && schema.maintains.iter().filter_map(|m|m.private.as_ref()).all(|o| schema.table(&o.table).is_some_and(|t|t.maintained.contains_key(&o.column))) { return Ok(()); }
    if schema.tables.values().any(|table| !table.maintained.is_empty())
        || schema.maintains.iter().any(|maintain| maintain.private.is_some())
    {
        return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_POSTGRES_MAINTAINED_COLUMN",
            message: "Postgres evaluation does not support maintained columns or their private maintains; use the SQLite engine for maintained columns (guide maintains)".into() });
    }
    Ok(())
}

//! Atomic adoption of the maintained-row address function in the evaluation
//! adapter. The marker and generation publish in the same writer transaction
//! as the target rebuild, so no writer can observe mixed legacy/digest ids.
use super::*;

pub(super) fn install(
    tx: &store::Tx<'_>,
    schema: &Schema,
    creating: bool,
    generation: u64,
) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
    let current = tx.query(
        "SELECT maintained_identity_version FROM _backend WHERE singleton",
        &[],
    )?[0].get::<_, Option<&str>>(0).map(str::to_owned);
    if current.as_deref() == Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION) {
        return Ok(generation);
    }

    let aggregates: Vec<_> = schema.maintains.iter()
        .filter(|maintain| maintain.row_key.is_none())
        .cloned()
        .collect();
    if !creating && !aggregates.is_empty() {
        let mut runner = Runner::new(
            tx,
            schema,
            Context::system().at(crate::now_ms()),
            Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort),
            tx.next_seq()?,
        );
        runner.event_free = true;
        runner.rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(&aggregates, None, None)?;
        for maintain in &aggregates {
            runner.rebuild_maintain(maintain)?;
        }
        // The narrow maintained-column shape admitted by this adapter keeps
        // its private target out of the public rows but still shares the same
        // identity upgrade. Rebuild every target before publishing the marker,
        // then restore its authoritative value into each live parent.
        // @ref LLP 3000.007.001#3.11 — activation is rebuild, then mirror, before the generation barrier.
        for maintain in aggregates.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_some()) {
            runner.mirror_column_pass(maintain)?;
        }
    }

    let generation = if creating || aggregates.is_empty() {
        generation
    } else {
        generation.checked_add(1)
            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Generation("generation overflow".into()))?
    };
    tx.execute(
        "UPDATE _backend SET maintained_identity_version=$1, generation=$2 WHERE singleton",
        &[&crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION, &store::signed(generation)?],
    )?;
    Ok(generation)
}

// Only this evaluator can manufacture expression-pricing authority. Store
// rows must pass project_row before entering its environment or result values.
pub(crate) struct ExpressionAccess(());

/// Minted only at the runner boundary; Context is data, never pricing authority.
pub(crate) struct SystemAccess(());
impl Runner<'_> {
    pub(super) fn system_access(&self) -> Option<SystemAccess> {
        self.context.is_system().then_some(SystemAccess(()))
    }
}
pub(super) fn expression_heap(value: &Value) -> u64 { value.expression_heap(ExpressionAccess(())) }
pub(super) fn expression_copy(value: &Value) -> u64 { value.expression_copy(ExpressionAccess(())) }

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]

    Continue,
    Return(Value),
}

/// What a commit's retirement of its already-expired births

    /// end: the order of removal must not reach a total no commit would hold.

    /// canonical key). Removing expired rows cannot change the answer, so each
    /// key is scanned once.
    pub(crate) live_keys: HashMap<(String, String, String), bool>,
}

/// A logless device still nets maintained deltas across commit-end expiry.
